coursesExamined.name: Personal & Professional Development

selectedEvidence.profile: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.

selectedEvidence.description2: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

selectedEvidence.profile: Introduces financial accounting, management accounting and investment appraisal, including accounting's social role and accountability implications. Students record transactions, prepare and interpret financial statements, and analyze performance and financing. The course then examines costing, pricing, budgeting, organizational control and sustainable management accounting. Investment decisions are evaluated using accounting and discounted-cash-flow measures. A case study analyzes the misuse of an accounting principle and its financial-statement effects.

Topics include trade regulation, contracts and international sales, transport and documentary transactions, finance, services, intellectual property, foreign investment and digital commerce. Advisory assignments assess contractual outcomes, risk allocation, intellectual-property protection and e-commerce compliance. A simulated arbitration develops written legal argument and oral advocacy.

coursesExamined.name: Money, Banking & Finance

selectedEvidence.profile: Examines financial markets and institutions, including the pricing of bonds, stocks and derivatives, interest rates and their risk and term structure, commercial-bank balance sheets and performance, financial structure and regulation, banking fragility and financial crises, central banks, money creation and monetary policy. Students apply algebraic and graphical analysis to financial and monetary problems. In the Stanford Banking Game they manage a simulated bank, analyse performance in Excel dashboards, forecast financial statements, and make evidence-based decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk. A small research project extends a selected financial or monetary research article through additional literature, a case study or updated evidence.

coursesExamined.name: Econometrics

selectedEvidence.description2: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

GOSSOCI215: social movements, environmental justice and civic engagement only as expressly stated.

academicJudgment: These are related legal-study responses, not Dutch professional degrees. Closest retains8substantive legal/rights courses (gateway, humanrights, criminal, private, constitutional, international, EU, businesslaw) and social/normative/empirical inquiry into legal order. The public option has6legal/rights courses with political institutions, historical power, public economy, policy-making and civil-society research; comparative private law replaces unsupported climate-persuasion-as-legal-skills while public-policy analysis replaces general negotiation and public authority remains its priority. The business option has8legal/rights courses with financial institutions, economic incentives, corporate governance, specific policy-making analysis and empirical evidence. Programme-level legal substance is sustained, not incidental. Lack of professional licensing alone is not a no-match basis.
boundedRepairs: Five original offering conflicts are case-specific, not systemic. Preserve sound external research and concepts. MCCCOMM311 removed from options2/3: climate and circular-lifestyle persuasion is too weakly tied to these proposed legal concepts; replace with actual comparative private law and public-policy inquiry respectively; replace general negotiation in the public option with directly relevant policy-making analysis. Actual differences are recomputed rather than inheriting incorrect legacy counts. Rhetoric remains only in option3 as a specific complementary analysis of forensic discourse and persuasive legal claims, not a legal-academic skills equivalence.
qualitativeDistinctness: Closest integrates legal fields with politics and sociology. Option2 shifts towards public and transnational authority, history and civic claims; criminal/business-law study gives way to this public emphasis. Option3 shifts to legal/economic organisation of commercial relationships, accounting/finance, governance and policy. Numerical differences support, but do not establish, these substantive distinctions.
alignmentFinding: All23components individually reassessed. Remove generic economics, rhetoric and persuasion alignments; retain confirmed moral-theory partial relationship, direct legal-field matches and business-law application. Prefer qualitative social inquiry over general statistics as the empirical-method counterpart. All other components remain explicit blank rows, not forced matches. Optional15ECresearch sits beside mandatory10ECskills/thesis once perUCRcolumn, excluded from180.
